reason: Quote and mechanism verify exactly: ShopConfigLoader.java:110-112 throws IllegalStateException whenever YamlFiles.Loaded.usable() is false, and YamlFiles.load quarantines then returns Loaded(null, SUSPECT/PARSE_FAILED/QUARANTINE_FAILED) for a blank, unparseable, or unmovable shop.yml (YamlFiles.java:88-93 and 139-151); ShopManager.reload() assigns loader.load() unguarded at ShopManager.java:56, and onEnable calls it at HilltopVillagePlugin.java:120 outside the catch(Throwable) blocks that wrap only PlayerGoodsManager/StatsManager (HilltopVillagePlugin.java:105-116). Paper disables a plugin whose onEnable throws, so 'takes the whole plugin down' is literally accurate rather than overstated, and the /hilltop shop reload path (HilltopCommandHandler.java:578-579) is equally unguarded. It is nevertheless a deliberate fail-closed design, not an oversight: HilltopVillagePlugin.java:103-104 states in-code that a core-module init failure should disable the plugin rather than continue half-initialized, ShopConfigLoader.java:86-89 says the throw is intentional, and ShopConfigCorruptFileTest and ShopConfigQuarantineRebuildTest both assert the throw. shop.yml has no plugin-side writer (grep for gate.write/YamlFiles.write/saveToString in the shop package returns nothing), so the trigger is confined to invalid hand-edited YAML or an external write interruption, the bad file is preserved as shop.yml.corrupt instead of being replaced or lost, and the thrown message names the file and the exact recovery step. 'high' overstates an availability-only, recoverable clean-disable caused by an admin config error whose whole purpose is to avoid silently replacing a live shop, so downgrade to medium; the residual real gap (no isolation and no admin-facing feedback on the runtime /hilltop shop reload path) is already carried by S09-F3 at the same line.
